title: Codex: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
hook: Fine-tune GPT on public GitHub code and you get a model that solves programming problems and powers GitHub Copilot - plus a new benchmark, HumanEval, that tests functional correctness.
key_points: GPT fine-tuned on hundreds of millions of lines of public GitHub code; code pretraining transfers to problem-solving.
Introduced HumanEval: 164 hand-written Python problems evaluated by running tests, not string matching.
The pass@k metric - generate k samples, pass if any one solves the problem - rewards sampling diverse solutions.
Formed the technical basis for GitHub Copilot, the first widely deployed AI coding assistant.
content_html: Chen and colleagues at OpenAI published Codex in July 2021, describing how fine-tuning a GPT-style model on public code produced a system capable of translating natural-language docstrings into working Python functions. The model became the engine behind GitHub Copilot and established HumanEval as the standard benchmark for measuring functional code generation.
extra_html:
How it works

Starting from a GPT language model pretrained on text, the authors continued training on a large corpus of Python code scraped from public GitHub repositories. At evaluation time, the model takes a function signature and docstring as a prompt and generates a completion. The HumanEval benchmark measures correctness by executing the generated code against a hidden test suite, not by comparing tokens - a meaningful shift from BLEU-based code evaluation. The pass@k metric counts a problem as solved if at least one of k generated samples passes all tests.

Why it matters

Codex reframed code generation from a research curiosity into a practical tool deployed at scale through GitHub Copilot. HumanEval and the pass@k metric became the standard yardstick that later models like AlphaCode and GPT-4 are measured against, anchoring a whole line of subsequent research. Read the full evaluation methodology in the paper on arXiv.

related.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real GitHub Issues?
related.hook: Test a coding agent on real GitHub issues with real test suites - not toy problems - and the bar turns out to be much harder than HumanEval suggested.
